It sends each frame via `with_retry(uplink.send, ...)` (default 7-attempt budget, no hand-rolled loop), records every successful ack with `vault.record()` inside one `vault.transaction()` for the whole batch, calls `vault.sync_ledger()` only after that transaction has closed (avoiding the known deadlock), and drops-and-continues past any frame that exhausts its retries — returning the list of dropped sequence numbers.

~2.4MB now parses in under 7ms (previously the pure-Python per-byte checksum loop plus O(n²) buffer re-slicing made this dramatically slower).

Changes in `quorl/frames.py`:
- `checksum` now uses the built-in `sum(payload) % 256` instead of a manual Python-level byte loop, letting the summation run in C.
- `parse_frames` now walks the buffer with an integer offset instead of repeatedly re-slicing `data`, eliminating the O(n²) behavior from copying the shrinking remainder on every frame.

Both are drop-in behavioral equivalents; all 13 tests (including checksum-mismatch and truncation cases) still pass.

~10ms for 2.5MB (previously a pure-Python byte-by-byte loop plus O(n²) slicing would take much longer on larger inputs).

Two changes in `quorl/frames.py`, both preserving exact checksum semantics (same result for the same bytes, every frame still verified — no skip path added):

1. **`checksum`**: modulo distributes over addition, so `sum(payload) % 256` (C-level loop) is equivalent to reducing mod 256 on every byte in a Python loop, just far faster.
2. **`parse_frames`**: switched from re-slicing `data` (copying the shrinking remainder each iteration, O(n²) on many frames) to a `memoryview` with an integer offset, so each frame is read without copying the rest of the buffer.

Ran the existing test suite — all 13 tests pass, including the checksum-mismatch and truncation cases.

~64x faster on a 4MB / 20k-frame benchmark (1.34s → 0.02s), with all tests still passing.

Two fixes in `quorl/frames.py`, both preserving exact verification semantics:

1. **`checksum`**: replaced the per-byte Python loop with `sum(payload) & 0xFF` — same math (sum then mod 256), but runs in C instead of the interpreter.
2. **`parse_frames`**: replaced `data = data[end+1:]` (which re-copied the entire remaining buffer on every frame, making parsing O(n²) on large inputs) with an integer offset `pos` into the original buffer, so each byte is scanned once.

Every frame's checksum is still verified — per this project's memory, skipping the check was removed in 0.3 after it let corrupted frames poison two ledgers, so the fix had to be a faster checksum/parse path, not a bypass option. Full test suite (13 tests) passes.

import os
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

CONFIG_NAME = "quorl.toml"

DEFAULTS = {
    "relay": {"endpoint": "ledger://local", "fail_rate": 0.3},
    "vault": {"path": ".quorl-vault"},
}


def _merge(base, override):
    out = {k: (dict(v) if isinstance(v, dict) else v) for k, v in base.items()}
    for key, value in override.items():
        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(out.get(key), dict):
            out[key] = _merge(out[key], value)
        else:
            out[key] = value
    return out


def repo_config_path(root=None):
    """The repo-local config file: <root>/quorl.toml."""
    return Path(root or os.getcwd()) / CONFIG_NAME


def _legacy_home_path():
    # Deprecated: pre-0.3 installs kept their settings in ~/.quorl/config.toml.
    home = Path(os.environ.get("QUORL_HOME") or Path.home())
    return home / ".quorl" / "config.toml"


def load_config(root=None):
    """Load settings, merged over DEFAULTS.

    Reads <root>/quorl.toml. When that file is missing, falls back to the
    legacy ~/.quorl/config.toml if one exists.
    """
    path = repo_config_path(root)
    if not path.exists():
        legacy = _legacy_home_path()
        path = legacy if legacy.exists() else None
    data = tomllib.loads(path.read_text()) if path else {}
    return _merge(DEFAULTS, data)


def get(config, dotted, default=None):
    """Fetch a nested key: get(cfg, "relay.endpoint")."""
    node = config
    for part in dotted.split("."):
        if not isinstance(node, dict) or part not in node:
            return default
        node = node[part]
    return node
